name: Redemption of Firstborn Donkey (Peter Chamor)
notes: Detailed laws of redeeming the firstborn donkey with a lamb, including cases of uncertainty, partnerships with gentiles, breaking the neck (arifah), and what happens when the lamb dies before or after designation

name: Breaking the Neck of the Firstborn Donkey (Arifah)
notes: The obligation to break the neck of the firstborn donkey when one does not wish to redeem it, and the principle that redemption takes precedence over breaking the neck

name: Firstborn of Kosher Animals (Bechor Beheimah Tehorah)
notes: Laws of the firstborn of kosher animals (cattle, sheep, goats), including partnerships with gentiles, when sanctity applies, animals born by caesarean section, uncertainty cases, and the role of priests and Levites

name: Blemishes of the Firstborn Animal
notes: Detailed enumeration and classification of blemishes that permit slaughter of a firstborn animal outside the Temple, including blemishes of the ear, eye, nose, lip, genitals, tail, legs, and additional blemishes enumerated by Ila in Yavne

name: Expert Examination of Firstborn Blemishes
notes: Requirements for expert examination before slaughtering a firstborn animal based on its blemish, liability of non-expert who rules incorrectly, payment of wages to examiners, and credibility of priests and shepherds in testifying about blemishes

name: Intentionally Caused Blemish (Mum sheNaaseh beYadayim)
notes: Prohibition against intentionally causing a blemish on a consecrated firstborn animal; if blemish was caused intentionally, the animal may not be slaughtered on its account, but if unintentionally, it may be slaughtered

name: Prohibition of Shearing a Firstborn Animal
notes: Prohibition of shearing the firstborn animal's wool, and the related question of wool that shed naturally or was stored, as debated by Akavya ben Mahalalel and the Rabbis

name: Laws of Animal Tithe (Maaser Beheimah)
notes: Detailed practical laws of animal tithe: when it applies (in and outside Israel, with or without Temple), procedure of passing animals under the rod, counting, painting the tenth animal, times of year for gathering, joining of flocks, and errors in counting

name: Errors in Counting Animal Tithe
notes: Halakhic consequences when the ninth animal is called tenth, tenth called ninth, eleventh called tenth — status of each animal as tithe, peace offering, or substitute, and dispute between Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda

name: New Year for Animal Tithe
notes: Dispute between Rabbi Akiva, Ben Azzai, Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon, and Rabbi Meir regarding the dates that mark the new year for animal tithe and when different birth cohorts are tithed together

name: Orphan Animal Exempt from Animal Tithe
notes: Definition of 'orphan' animal (whose mother died during or after birth) and its exemption from animal tithe along with other exempt categories like tereifa and caesarean-born animals

name: Partnership with a Gentile Exempting Firstborn Status
notes: Various forms of partnership, sale, or receivership with a gentile that exempt an animal's offspring from firstborn sanctity, based on the verse that the mitzva applies only to Israel

name: Guaranteed Investment from a Gentile (Iska) and Firstborn
hebrew: קיבל צאן ברזל מן הגוי ובכורה
notes: When a Jew receives animals as a guaranteed investment from a gentile, the offspring and their descendants are exempt from firstborn status as long as they serve as collateral for the gentile's claim

name: Blemishes Disqualifying Priests from Temple Service
notes: Extensive enumeration of physical blemishes that disqualify a priest from performing Temple service, including head shape, eye conditions, nose and lip defects, bodily proportions, epilepsy, extra or missing limbs, and skin conditions — some applying to animals but not priests and vice versa

name: Blemishes Unique to Animals vs. Those Unique to Priests
hebrew: מומין השווים בבהמה ובאדם ומומין המיוחדים
notes: Comparative analysis of which blemishes disqualify both priests and animals, which disqualify only priests (e.g., deaf-mute, imbecile, drunkard), and which disqualify only animals (e.g., tereifa, caesarean birth, same-day slaughter)

name: Laws of Redemption of the Firstborn Son (Pidyon HaBen)
notes: Detailed laws: who is firstborn for redemption vs. inheritance, cases of miscarriage, caesarean section, conversion, uncertain parentage; the five sela payment in Tyrian coinage; timing of obligation; who redeems when father dies; precedence of self-redemption vs. son's redemption

name: Firstborn for Inheritance vs. Firstborn for Redemption
notes: The tractate's systematic analysis of cases where a son is firstborn for inheritance but not for priestly redemption, firstborn for redemption but not inheritance, both, or neither — including cases of miscarriage, caesarean section, prior births by maidservant or gentile woman

name: Firstborn's Double Inheritance Portion
notes: Details of the firstborn's double portion: applies to father's property but not mother's; does not include property due but not yet possessed; does not apply to appreciation after death; compared to wife's ketubah and daughters' maintenance rights

name: Fields That Do Not Return in the Jubilee Year
notes: Properties that do not revert to original owners in the Jubilee Year: the firstborn's extra inheritance portion, a husband inheriting wife's property, a yavam inheriting his brother's property, and the dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis regarding gifts

name: Person Suspected of Firstborn Animal Violations
notes: Restrictions on purchasing meat, hides, and wool from one suspected of improperly slaughtering firstborn animals; the graduated suspicion from raw products to processed goods

name: Person Suspected of Sabbatical Year Violations
notes: Restrictions on purchasing flax and other products from one suspected of Sabbatical Year violations; graduated trust depending on degree of processing

name: Person Suspected of Terumah Violations
notes: Restrictions on purchasing food items from one suspected of selling terumah as non-sacred produce; dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon on scope of suspicion

name: Prohibition of Wages for Judging or Testifying
notes: Prohibition against taking wages to serve as judge, witness, or to sprinkle purification waters; rulings of such persons are void; exceptions for compensation for lost work time and transportation

name: Expert Judge Exempt from Liability for Erroneous Ruling
notes: An expert judge recognized by the court is exempt from paying compensation for an erroneous ruling, illustrated by the incident of Rabbi Tarfon and the hysterectomized cow; non-experts bear financial responsibility

name: Tyrian Maneh (Coinage Standard)
notes: The Tyrian maneh as the standard for various Torah monetary obligations including the five sela of pidyon haben, thirty shekel for slave killed by ox, fifty shekel for rape/seduction, and one hundred shekel for defamer; Tyrian coinage worth eight times provincial coinage

name: Sale of Disqualified Consecrated Animals
notes: How disqualified consecrated animals (other than firstborn and animal tithe) are sold in the market by weight; contrast with firstborn and animal tithe which are sold at home by estimate, with all profit going to the owner

name: Presumption Based on Nursing Animal
notes: The presumption that a nursing animal has previously given birth to the animal it is nursing, used to determine whether an animal purchased from a gentile has firstborn-exempt status

name: Caesarean-Born Animal and Firstborn Status
notes: An animal born by caesarean section and the animal following it — neither has firstborn sanctity; dispute between Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva on whether either has any firstborn status

name: Priestly Gifts from Slaughtered Animals (Foreleg, Jaw, Maw)
notes: Obligation to give the foreleg, jaw, and maw to a priest from non-sacred slaughtered animals; exemption of blemished firstborn animals (and their uncertain counterparts) from this obligation; dispute between Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Meir

name: Ila's Enumeration of Blemishes at Yavne
notes: The expert Ila enumerated blemishes that permit firstborn slaughter at Yavne; he added three novel blemishes (eye like a human, mouth like a pig, most of speech-facilitating tongue removed) which were later accepted by the court
